description:
The authorized fz-kdt.119 Scope-A carve-out, made a ticket per the
scaffolding law: under Scope A, nested list positions inside tuple
shapes report ERASING in overlaps_on_an_erasing_axis and their
sub-predicates stay shape-only -- because making them exact REACHES
the dead-and-broken accumulator specialization (fz-kdt.132, the
blocker: 'backend callable construction 27 matched no member' on
enum_take_drop_split -- P1<->P3 prototype delta proved the boundary is
exactly nested lists). When 132 lands, lift the carve-out: nested
list sub-predicates become as exact as the list axis itself supports
(which is still shape-only until fz-kdt.107 step 3 gives lists
element discrimination -- so this ticket may collapse into 107 step 3
if that lands first; check before building). Re-run the 119 census
instruments and the surface-membership tripwire on lift.

comments.text:
UNBLOCKED-BY-DESIGN by fz-kdt.119 (4ca1dc7e7): Scope B is now a ONE-LINE change plus its consequences.

runtime_type_predicate::lowering_tests_position is the single place the carve-out lives -- `sub.lists.is_none()` -- and everything else already reads it: position_overlaps, position_erases and position_contains in the lattice, emit_shapes_of_arity in the shared native emitter, matches_tuple_shape in the interpreter, and emit_delivered_tuple_test on the destination-passing path. Making it `true` turns the list axis on at every one of them at once.

What lands with the flip: the list positions stop being erasing, so seats gain separation there; the fz-kdt.132 specialization becomes reachable and must be correct first (that is the block); and the tripwire baseline should drop by the 212 occurrences the two enum_take_drop_split paths hold today (see fz-kdt.135's baseline), which is the measurement that says Scope B worked.

Acceptance reproducer from the fz-kdt.119 refutation (F2, pre-existing at base, all three doors): fn f(x :: {:a, [integer]}), do: 1 / fn f(x :: {:a, integer}), do: 2 -- prints 1 1 (Elixir: 1 2); swap the clauses and the sibling shape prints 2 2. The fixed P1's verbatim twin at any list-bearing position. The fz-kdt.135 tripwire fires on it exactly once (good acceptance signal). This ticket's framing grows: not just the internal accumulator cost -- user-visible clause dispatch is wrong at list positions until this lands.

fz-kdt.107 step-3 review (2026-09-01, answers this ticket's own check-question): 138 does NOT collapse into 107 step 3 -- measured with the full step-3 prototype built, F2 still prints 1 1; the carve-out is still sub.lists-based and this one-line flip remains F2's SOLE cure. Orthogonal to 107.3 (either lands first); still blocked by fz-kdt.132 (the flip immediately breaks take_drop/00420, reproduced). ALSO yours on landing: the tripwire baseline drops by the 212 take_drop occurrences.

UNBLOCKED at fz-kdt.132 (c31b309d0). Verified by probe, not by inference: the one-line flip of runtime_type_predicate::lowering_tests_position to `true` was applied at HEAD and both target fixtures were run on all three doors.

BEFORE (base + flip, at 8002889ff): 00420 and behavior/enum_take_drop_split both fail -- interp 'backend callable construction 27 matched no member', JIT and AOT 'function_clause: ... halted through a fault trap'.
AFTER (fix + flip): both fixtures print the expected output byte-for-byte on interp, JIT and AOT.

The probe was then REVERTED; this ticket still owns the flip and its consequences. Also yours on landing, and now free: the surface-membership tripwire baseline is already 0 corpus-wide at HEAD (fz-kdt.132 emptied it -- the 212 take_drop occurrences and the other 56 were all one missing accumulator rung), so 'the baseline drops by the 212' is spent. The measurement that says Scope B worked is now the F2 reproducer from the fz-kdt.119 refutation: fn f(x :: {:a, [integer]}) / fn f(x :: {:a, integer}) must print 1 2, not 1 1. Re-run the 119 census instruments on lift as planned.

RE-SCOPED by the fz-kdt.132 refutation (2026-09-02): BOTH acceptance signals are spent -- the tripwire baseline is 0 (132 emptied it) and the F2 reproducer prints 1 2 at head AND base, both clause orders (closed at or before fz-kdt.107's landing; the earlier 1 1 record was measured against the step-3 PROTOTYPE base). The flip itself is now measured ZERO-MOVER corpus-wide (585 fixtures, census 0, behaviour identical, take_drop three doors green). THE HONEST RE-SCOPE: if nothing observable changes under the flip, the carve-out no longer protects anything -- this ticket becomes a RIP-OUT (delete lowering_tests_position's list-blinding and whatever exists only to serve it) with acceptance = zero movement everywhere + the deleted code, NOT a defect fix. Before building: find ANY program the flip changes (the 132 refuter could not); if none exists, land as the deletion; if one exists, it is the new red-first gate.

LANDED as CASE 2 -- a DEFECT FIX, not the rip-out. ce6768af4.

THE RE-SCOPE'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, and here is why the 132 refuter could not
see it. Both of its negative measurements were probe artifacts:

1. THE F2 REPRODUCER WAS MEASURED WITH LITERAL ARGUMENTS. `f({:a, [1]})` /
   `f({:a, 1})` prints 1 2 at base because the argument's own type settles the
   clause at COMPILE TIME -- no runtime dispatch is reached at all. Route the
   same value through an unfoldable producer (`pick(n)`, the technique
   dispatch_annotated_tuple_tag_clauses and dispatch_list_head_separates both
   use) and base prints 1 1. Measured at 81ec3f25d on all three doors.

2. "ZERO-MOVER CORPUS-WIDE" IS TRUE AND MEANS NOTHING. No corpus fixture
   writes a list-bearing tuple position with two clauses that need separating.
   Re-measured here: 585 existing fixtures, 0 behaviour movers on interp, JIT
   and AOT. The population is empty; the defect is not.

DISCRIMINATOR HUNT -- every shape tried, base vs flip, `interp` first then all
three doors. `pick` indirection throughout.

  p1  {:a, [integer]}         vs {:a, [:ok | :err]}          RED 1 1 / 2 2
  p2  {:a, []}                vs {:a, [integer]}             RED 1 1
  p2b {:a, [integer]}         vs {:a, []}                    green (containment)
  p3  {:a, [integer]}         vs {:a, integer}               RED 1 1 (fwd order)
  p3lit  same, literal args                                  green (folded)
  p7  {:a, {:b, [integer]}}   vs {:a, {:b, [:ok | :err]}}    RED 1 1 / 2 2
  p8  {[integer], [:ok|:err]} vs {[:ok|:err], [integer]}     RED 1 1 / 2 2
  lit  p1+p2+p7 shapes, literal args                         green (folded)

FOUR independent red shapes, on interp, JIT and AOT alike. p2b is green on
purpose: `[]` is contained in `[integer]` (a list type is `[]` joined with the
lists over its element), so seating the wide clause first is Elixir's answer
too -- only narrow-first is a question the blind position can get wrong.

RED-FIRST GATE: fixtures2/behavior/dispatch_nested_list_position_separates.fz
carries all four shapes, both clause orders where the pair is disjoint, with
an Elixir oracle. Red at 81ec3f25d on three doors; green after, byte-for-byte
against the oracle, and invariant under all twelve FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH
settings on all three doors.

THE FIX is the flip made permanent as a DELETION: `lowering_tests_position`
and the three lattice wrappers that existed only to consult it
(position_overlaps / position_erases / position_contains) are gone, and so are
the two `continue` branches in runtime_test.rs's shared emitter and prim.rs's
destination-passing path. The lattice asks positions directly.

ARTIFACT MOVEMENT, classified. Canon comparand over 586 fixtures: THREE movers,
all receive fixtures (receive_interleaved_tuple_arity, receive_list_cons_pattern,
receive_map_pattern), all behaviour-identical, all the SAME movement -- same 8
bodies, same 14/17 arms, identical question multiset, seat rotated by one: the
fully-constrained `{:unknown, :unknown, :unknown}` arm moves from last to
first. That is `specificity_order`'s precision preference finally able to see
a strict containment that `position_contains` had been answering `true` for
unconditionally. An improvement, not a regression.

CONSEQUENCE FOR fz-kdt.135's TRIPWIRE (commented on 135 and 144): after this,
PositionScope::Lowered and ::Full are the same function, so `escaped()` is
`X && !X`. The census still reads 0 corpus-wide, but now BY CONSTRUCTION
rather than by measurement. The plumbing is kept and re-documented as such
because fz-kdt.144's list-TAIL re-ask is what gives `Full` content again --
deleting it would make 144 rebuild the instrument.

GATES: lib 1571/0/5 (two carve-out unit tests rewritten to the new fact, one
of them widened to three claims incl. the one-sided-filter law holding INSIDE
a position), cli 24/0, matrix --test-threads=1 452/0/9 (449 + the new
fixture's three doors), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, release clean.
Corpus sweeps interp/JIT/AOT 586 fixtures 1 mover (the new fixture). Tripwire
0 corpus-wide. FIFO vs LIFO byte-identical on all four schedule lenses and on
the new fixture; corpus dump census unchanged at the same three schedule-movers
(00277_enum_tier0_fixture, dead_closure_capture_empty_list, enum_map_family).
Two-process canon determinism holds on the movers. Blind-escape census
unchanged at 3.

title: Scope B of the tuple-shape predicate: nested LIST positions stop erasing
